title: Compact SDK starter repo + hybrid examples: Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI (retries & streaming ergonomics)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a small, opinionated starter repository and cookbook snippets that demonstrate a production-appropriate integration pattern for Redwood SDKs across Next.js (TS), FastAPI (Python), Go HTTP server, and a CLI. Focus areas: consistent retry semantics, streaming ergonomics (server & client patterns), minimal onboarding DX, and a single lightweight monorepo layout that teams can fork and adapt. This ticket covers scaffolding, sample code that showcases best-practice retry/backoff (idempotency keys, idempotent vs. non-idempotent calls), streaming consumption patterns (server-sent events vs. chunked HTTP vs. SDK streaming helpers), CI linting, and an onboarding README with cookbook snippets for common patterns (prompt caching, prefix caching, abort signals).
acceptance_criteria: A single monorepo `examples/sdks-starters` containing Next.js app, FastAPI app, Go HTTP server, and a small CLI; each app has a README and minimal Dockerfile
Language-specific examples demonstrate retry/backoff + idempotency: each repo shows how to set idempotency keys and when to use exponential vs. linear backoff

Streaming examples include both server-driven streaming (FastAPI with event-stream), client streaming consumption (Next.js using fetch streams and SDK stream helper), and Go streaming reader using a cancellations/ctx pattern
All examples use the same environment config format (.env.example) and a short script to run locally with minimal setup
Automated lint / basic unit smoke tests run in CI and pass on PRs
Documentation: README includes cookbook snippets for 6 patterns: retries, streaming client, streaming server, CLI batching, caching/prefix usage, and error handling with fallbacks
PR with implementation merged and a follow-on internal doc/Confluence page linked in comments
tasks: Scaffold monorepo structure + minimal build/run scripts
Implement Next.js demo route: streaming chat using SDK streaming helper + reconnect guidance
Implement FastAPI demo: streaming SSE endpoint, example of prefix cache and KV caching usage
Implement Go HTTP sample: long-poll vs streaming, proper context cancellation and backpressure handling
Implement CLI sample: batch mode and interactive mode, show retries with exponential backoff and idempotency key option
Add .env.example and local-start script that uses docker compose where appropriate
Add CI workflow: install, lint, run smoke tests for each language
Write README + cookbook snippets + migration notes for existing starter repos
implementation_notes: Design choices: prefer explicit SDK stream helpers over raw fetch for Next.js to keep pattern stable across runtimes. Use idempotency-key header name `x-redwood-idempotency` in examples. Retries: recommend default client retry policy of 3 attempts with jittered exponential backoff (base 300ms). For streaming endpoints, show pattern using an initial non-streaming handshake to detect model variant and fall back to non-streaming endpoint on network/cardinality failures. Keep examples minimal (<= 200 SLoC per app). Note: do not include secrets in repo; use .env and instructions pointing to Redwood Console tokens.
